purpose: Teach: 一途/沈む/バケツ/下町/花びら/散っ/微笑ん/快く

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、ばあさんに、一途だったよな、私、覚えてる、本当に、ロマンチックだったわよね。
lines.en: When I was young, I remember how devoted I was to you. You used to say I was truly romantic.
lines.style: Soft nostalgic opening. Voice distant with time. Gentle, searching — as if speaking to someone he's known forever. Pause before 'romantic' like he's still a little amazed at himself.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん。夕日が、沈むのを、二人で、よく、見たわよね、覚えてる、あなた、本当に、思い出。
lines.en: Yes. We'd often watch the sunset together, remember? So many memories like that.
lines.style: Warm, reaching back. Not performing memory — living in it. Her voice finds steadiness in the familiar detail. Slight upward lilt on 'remember?' like she's checking that he's there with her.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 昔の井戸、バケツで、水、汲んでたよな、本当に、苦労した時代だった、ばあさん。
lines.en: The old well — I remember drawing water with the bucket. Those were hard times, weren't they?
lines.style: Steady, deliberate cadence. Voice carries the weight of what he's remembering without complaint. Almost reverent about it. Pause before 'hard times' — not seeking pity, just stating fact.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 下町で、子育てしたわよね、私たち、本当に、思い出が、いっぱい、あるわよね、覚えてる?
lines.en: We raised our children in that downtown neighborhood. So many memories we built together. Do you remember?
lines.style: Conversational but reaching. She's not just recounting — she's asking him to walk through it with her. Warm undertone. The 'remember?' is gentle, not urgent.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 庭の桜、花びら、散ってしまったな、ばあさん、また、来年、楽しみだな、二人で、見ようね。
lines.en: The cherry blossoms in the garden have all fallen now. But next year will come again, won't it? Let's watch them together.
lines.style: Quiet acceptance of passage. No sadness at the petals falling — just natural observation. Slight brightening on 'next year.' The 'let's watch together' is tender promise, not wistfulness.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 孫が、微笑んでくれる、その顔、本当に、宝物よね、あなた、毎日、思い出すわよ、私。
lines.en: Our grandchild's smile — that face — is like a treasure to me. Every day I remember it, you know.
lines.style: Voice catches with genuine warmth. She's not performing sentiment; this is real gratitude that still surprises her. Soft, almost private. Slow on 'treasure.' Small laugh underneath.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 隣のおばさん、いつも、快く、お互いに、助け合ってきたわよな、ばあさん、本当に、ありがたい。
lines.en: Our neighbor next door — she's always helped us both so readily over the years. We're truly grateful for her kindness.
lines.style: Generous and clear. Not sentimental — just matter-of-fact warmth about someone who was simply there. Voice steady and sure. Slight nod of respect in his tone.
